text.title: clean-architecture Failure Modes
text.summary: Failure modes observed when applying the clean-architecture methodology. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Two critical violations: business logic in controllers, and ORM/framework imports inside domain entities.

antipattern.symptom: Email-uniqueness check lives in the controller; cannot be reused from CLI. Controller method contains business logic (email uniqueness check, direct entity construction) instead of delegating to a use case.
antipattern.root-cause: Author skipped the use-case step. Logic in controllers cannot be reused across delivery mechanisms (CLI, event handler, gRPC). Testing requires a running HTTP server. The same rule ends up duplicated in multiple endpoints.
antipattern.fix: Move logic to a use case; controller calls the use case. Code: see "Antipatterns in code" in content/05-examples.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Domain entity inherits from SQLAlchemy declarative base or imports ORM columns directly.
antipattern.root-cause: Author conflated entity with persistence model. The domain entity becomes tied to a specific ORM. Unit tests require a database. Migrating to a different database or ORM forces changes to business rules.
antipattern.fix: Define a plain dataclass entity; map to SQLAlchemy in infrastructure. Code: see "Antipatterns in code" in content/05-examples.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Dependency rule documented but no import-linter contract; violations accrue silently.
antipattern.fix: Add import-linter / ArchUnit contract; run on every PR.

antipattern.symptom: Application imports infrastructure for a 'temporary' DI shim.
antipattern.fix: Define the interface in domain/application; infrastructure implements; wire at composition root.
